title: P2RBox: Point Prompt Oriented Object Detection with SAM
summary: Single-point annotation in oriented object detection of remote sensing scenarios is gaining increasing attention due to its cost-effectiveness.However, due to the granularity ambiguity of points, there is a significant performance gap between previous methods and those with fully supervision. In this study, we introduce P2RBox, which employs point prompt to generate rotated box (RBox) annotation for oriented object detection. P2RBox employs the SAM model to generate high-quality mask proposals. These proposals are then refined using the semantic and spatial information from annotation points. The best masks are converted into oriented boxes based on the feature directions suggested by the model. P2RBox incorporates two advanced guidance cues: Boundary Sensitive Mask guidance, which leverages semantic information, and Centrality guidance, which utilizes spatial information to reduce granularity ambiguity. This combination enhances detection capabilities significantly.To demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, enhancements based on the baseline were observed by integrating three different detectors. Furthermore, compared to the state-of-the-art point-annotated generative method PointOBB, P2RBox outperforms by about 29% mAP (62.43% vs 33.31%) on DOTA-v1.0 dataset,which provides possibilities for the practical application of point annotations.

title: A Unified Multisensor Machine-Learning Framework for Live Fuel Moisture Content Retrieval
summary: Live fuel moisture content (LFMC) influences vegetation flammability, but field measurements are too sparse to describe its variation over large areas. We present, to our knowledge, the first LFMC framework that combines observations from multiple optical satellite sensors within the same trained models. More than two decades of GlobeLFMC 2.0 measurements are matched to Terra and Aqua Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), Landsat 8/9, Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3. We screen the vegetation surrounding sampling locations and adjust reflectance for differences between sensors before calculating vegetation indices. Weather, topography and time of year provide additional information. Separate models are trained for grasses, shrubs and trees. We test prediction on dates not used for training at sites where other dates contribute to training. At each site, records using the same satellite image are kept in either the training or the test set. The final Random Forest models achieve R2 values of 0.715, 0.693 and 0.691, respectively. Models trained on the combined archive give higher R2 and lower root mean square error than models trained on one satellite product in all 18 product–vegetation comparisons on identical test observations. Paired 95% confidence intervals support the improvement in 16 comparisons. Testing at sites excluded from training gives lower accuracy. The method produces LFMC maps at the selected satellite product’s resolution, from 20–30 m to 300–500 m.

title: Ground Clutter Filtering in Reflectivity-Only Weather Radar Remote Sensing Imagery: Event-Grouped Learning with Auxiliary Gauge Validation
summary: Ground clutter persists as residual stationary or recurrent echo in gridded reflectivity-only weather radar products, then is converted into spurious light rainfall when reflectivity is mapped to rain rate. This study presents an image-level quality control filter for Météo-France MeteoNet composites from northwestern France. Trained annotators labeled 346,629 pixels from clear-air and weather windows; complete events were withheld from training during validation. Intensity, spatial, temporal, and object features were combined in a random forest (RF) that separated clutter from weather echo on unseen events, reaching F1 = 0.833 with weather echo preservation of 0.952 and clutter suppression of 0.763. Choosing a 95% preservation operating point from training events alone maintained 0.953 preservation on outer test events; a gradient-boosted decision tree model achieved comparable discrimination. Rain gauges supported period screening, station-level recurrence review, and paired 30-min quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE). At nine reviewed recurrent-echo stations, targeted RF gating reduced false alarm ratio from 0.277 to 0.211 and mean absolute error from 0.0549 to 0.0526 mm by filtering the light rain echoes that produced false precipitation, while retaining most genuine rainfall. A mixed-echo analysis preserved 0.961 of overlapping labeled pixels, and a model trained only on 2016 data transferred to a 2017 test day with reduced error at the same stations. The resulting framework filters false precipitation effectively at locations with recurrent clutter, providing an auditable event-grouped workflow for quality control of reflectivity-only radar imagery.

title: Planetary Wave Forcing of Ozone Anomalies During 2024 Antarctic Stratospheric Warming
summary: Sudden Stratospheric Warmings (SSWs) are rare polar stratospheric extremes far less documented over Antarctica than the Arctic. A pair of successive midwinter Antarctic SSWs occurred in July–August 2024, featuring severe polar vortex distortion and sharp stratospheric temperature rises. Using MERRA-2/ERA5 reanalysis and Aura MLS satellite ozone data, we diagnose wave 1 and wave 2 planetary wave forcing and associated ozone variations. Abnormally strong upward-propagating Southern Hemisphere tropospheric planetary waves drove the 2024 SSW. Wave 1 triggered the first July warming peak, while amplified wave 2 dominated the second intense vortex disruption in early August. These waves delivered westward momentum that weakened the polar night jet and destabilized the vortex. Accelerated Brewer–Dobson circulation (BDC) enhanced poleward ozone transport, raising polar ozone levels and supplying extra stratospheric heat. Wave–ozone coupling shows clear selectivity: wave 1 induces negative total ozone column anomalies across 15°S–50°S midlatitudes, whereas wave 2 generates broad positive ozone signals over 50°S–65°S and primarily controls polar ozone enrichment. Fading planetary wave activity after the warming peaks gradually restored the polar vortex and stratospheric thermal structure. This study provides key observational evidence for rare Antarctic SSWs and advances understanding of stratosphere–troposphere coupling and polar ozone dynamics under global warming.

title: A Domain-Specific Memory Bank-Enhanced Framework for Remote Sensing Image Captioning
summary: Remote sensing image captioning enables automated interpretation of remote sensing data for applications such as environmental monitoring and urban planning. However, general-purpose multimodal models exhibit suboptimal adaptability on remote sensing imagery due to domain discrepancies in data distribution, resolution, and rotation invariance. We propose a domain-specific memory bank-enhanced framework for remote sensing image caption, built upon the lightweight EVCap architecture with three core innovations: (1) a remote sensing specific visual memory bank providing domain-representative visual-semantic alignment; (2) a staged transfer training strategy that leverages pre-trained knowledge while mitigating overfitting from limited remote sensing data; and (3) a K-means clustering-based few-shot memory bank that preserves performance while reducing memory footprint for resource-constrained deployment. Extensive experiments on NWPU, RSICD, and Sydney datasets demonstrate substantial improvements over baselines. Specifically, CIDEr increases by 3.3% on RSICD (0.2735 to 0.2825) and 11.7% on Sydney (0.1422 to 0.1589). The proposed method also achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods while maintaining favorable computational efficiency.

title: A Parameter-Compact Network with Hierarchical Detail Enhancement and High-Resolution Multiscale Fusion for Small Object Detection in UAV Imagery
summary: Small-object detection in UAV imagery remains challenging because repeated downsampling weakens fine structural cues, conventional feature pyramids are poorly aligned with small-object-dominated scale distributions, and fixed detection heads provide limited adaptation. To address these issues, a Hierarchical–Bidirectional–Dynamic Network (HBD-Net) is developed as a parameter-compact detector based on YOLOv11s. HEEM reinforces edge, contour, and texture information at multiple backbone stages using orthogonal depthwise strip convolutions, residual detail extraction, and zero-initialized fusion. PLSS replaces the conventional P3–P5 hierarchy with P2–P4 to emphasize high-resolution features, while P2-BiFPN introduces bidirectional propagation and learnable weighted fusion. An integrated Dynamic Head further refines features across scale, spatial, and task dimensions. On VisDrone, HBD-Net achieves 39.0% mAP50 and 22.6% mAP50–95, improving the YOLOv11s baseline by 6.9 and 4.3 percentage points, respectively, while reducing parameters from 9.4 M to 3.7 M. Ablation studies confirm the complementary effects of the components. On HIT-UAV, HBD-Net reaches 84.1% mAP50 and 57.0% mAP50–95, indicating effectiveness under infrared aerial imaging. These results demonstrate that coordinated structural enhancement, high-resolution multiscale fusion, and adaptive prediction can improve UAV small-object detection with a compact parameter footprint.

title: Bidirectional Global-Edge Refinement Network for Aerial Infrared Segmentation in Automated Industrial Inspection
summary: Accurate aircraft-region segmentation in aerial infrared imagery can provide a useful scene-understanding component for image-assisted aviation inspection. However, target scale variation and ambiguous boundaries remain challenging in simulated aerial infrared scenes. To address these issues, this paper develops a bidirectional collaborative framework that couples global semantic fusion with edge optimization. The Semantics-guided Multi-scale Context Fusion branch uses adaptive multi-scale feature extraction and cross-stage calibration to produce a reliable initial segmentation, while the Edge-Sensitive Superpixel Collaborative Refinement branch improves boundary localization through semantic-guided superpixel consistency. Their interaction forms a bidirectional closed loop in which semantic context guides edge refinement and refined boundaries feed back to semantic learning. Experiments on AISD, a dedicated physics-based simulated aerial infrared dataset, achieve an 86.29% mPA, 83.35% mF1, and 76.20% mIoU. Relative to the strongest baseline, P-Mamba, the gains are 0.89 percentage points in mPA, 1.52 points in mF1, and 0.88 points in mIoU, and a sourcewise holdout comparison indicates consistent performance under unseen source content within the AISD simulation pipeline. These results concern aircraft-region segmentation rather than direct diagnosis of thermal defects.

title: Range-Subband Processing for Range Spectrum Aliasing Suppression in Squinted Multi-Channel Spaceborne SAR
summary: Squinted multi-channel spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers wide-swath coverage and flexible observation geometry. However, imaging algorithms based on chirp scaling (CS) may broaden the range spectrum beyond the available sampling bandwidth, causing range spectrum aliasing and degrading the imaging quality of targets at the range edges of wide-swath scenes. To address this problem, this paper proposes a range-subband imaging method. First, a range spectrum broadening model is established to identify the main factors affecting spectral broadening. A subband division criterion is then derived to determine the minimum number of subbands required to avoid aliasing. Finally, a processing procedure comprising range-subband division, individual subband focusing, and coherent fusion is developed to recover the full-band range-focused signal. Point-target and distributed-target simulations verify that the proposed method suppresses range-spectrum aliasing and preserves full-band range resolution, while a broadside airborne experiment confirms that it introduces no appreciable image-quality degradation.

title: GeoPROV: A Semantic Provenance Profile for Coastal EO-Derived Products Informed by a Systematic Review of Spatial Data Supply Chains
summary: Emerging remote sensing technologies increasingly support coastal observation through Earth observation (EO) derivatives such as satellite-derived shorelines, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)- and light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-based elevation models, coastal land-use/land-cover products, bathymetric grids, turbidity and chlorophyll-a indicators, habitat maps, flood extents, and artificial intelligence (AI)-generated segmentation outputs. These EO-derived products are central to shoreline monitoring, coastal vulnerability assessment, flood-response planning, marine ecosystem management, and land–sea administration. Yet their evidential value depends on transparent provenance: users must know which sensor, acquisition condition, preprocessing chain, algorithm, model version, validation dataset, and uncertainty estimate produced each coastal product. The review synthesises 156 eligible publications identified through a systematic review process. Of these, 89 studies containing sufficient implementation and methodological detail were selected for detailed analytical coding. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) protocol, the review analyses application domains, provenance capture modes, representation strategies, semantic web technologies, and interoperability practices. A coastal EO thematic refinement translates the review findings into provenance requirements for satellite, UAV, LiDAR, Internet of Things (IoT), open-water, and AI-enabled coastal observation workflows. The review identifies persistent gaps in feature-level lineage, alignment between the World Wide Web Consortium Provenance Ontology (PROV-O) and International Organization for Standardization (ISO) geospatial metadata standards, spatial semantics, AI workflow transparency, uncertainty traceability, and scalable querying. To address these limitations, the paper introduces GeoPROV, a lightweight semantic profile of PROV-O designed for spatially explicit, feature-level provenance. GeoPROV aligns PROV-O with ISO 19115/19157, GeoSPARQL, Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL), and SpatioTemporal Asset Catalogue (STAC)-compatible catalogue practices. The framework enables EO-derived coastal products to be traced from raw observation through preprocessing, AI/geoprocessing, validation, catalogue publication, and coastal-administrative decision-making. The resulting GeoPROV profile integrates PROV-O, GeoSPARQL, SHACL, ISO 19115/19157 lineage concepts, and STAC metadata within a lightweight semantic framework demonstrated through a coastal EO product workflow and machine-actionable provenance implementation.

title: OEI-GTCD: An Object-Based Ecological Index-Driven Framework for Detecting Long-Term Disturbance–Recovery Trajectories in Mining Areas
summary: Ecological changes in mining areas are characterized by long-term dynamics, temporal stages, and spatial heterogeneity. Existing monitoring methods often face challenges in balancing multidimensional ecological condition characterization with spatially consistent analysis and have limited capability to identify complex disturbance–recovery trajectories. To address these issues, an Object-based Ecological Index-driven Framework (OEI-GTCD) is proposed to monitor ecological disturbance and recovery trajectories in mining areas. The framework uses the Mining-area Ecological Index (MEI) to characterize multidimensional ecological conditions and conducts analysis based on spatially consistent object units. On this basis, a Globally Optimized Time-series Change Detection method (GTCD) is proposed to improve the identification of complex ecological disturbance–recovery trajectories by integrating trend-change detection, abrupt-change detection, and segmentation optimization. Landsat imagery from 2000 to 2024 was used to characterize the spatiotemporal patterns of ecological disturbance and recovery across the Daye Mining Area, China. The findings suggest that MEI captures multiple dimensions of ecological conditions, while object-scale analysis characterizes ecological changes through overall object-level trajectories, supporting their spatial interpretation. OEI-GTCD achieved disturbance and recovery detection accuracies of 88.4% and 84.8%, respectively, representing improvements of 6.0 and 5.2 percentage points over OEI-LandTrendr. Ablation analyses further highlighted the contributions of abrupt-change detection and the improved segmentation criterion to event identification, as well as the role of local breakpoint refinement in temporal localization. From 2000 to 2024, stable and continuously improving ecological states together accounted for 82.07% of the area represented by the non-water objects used in the ecological analysis, while disturbance and recovery processes exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity. Overall, OEI-GTCD provides an integrated approach for monitoring ecological disturbance and recovery and characterizing their spatiotemporal patterns in mining areas.

title: Measuring Smooth Stone: Effects of Surface Texture on SfM Photogrammetry and Handheld 3D Scanning for Ancient-Vessel Metrology
summary: The accuracy of 3D digitisation methods is strongly influenced by the surface properties of the observed object, particularly its texture, reflectance, and material structure. This is especially relevant to the systematic metrological analysis of ancient stone vessels undertaken by the Artifact Research Foundation, where high-resolution 3D models are increasingly used for geometric analysis, including through dedicated tools such as Petrie Scope. This study assesses the potential influence of crystalline granite texture on residual dispersion in Structure-from-Motion (SfM) photogrammetry and handheld laser-triangulation scanning using granite metrological reference objects measured under controlled conditions before and after application of a self-sublimating scanning spray. For the unsprayed cube, the pooled empirical 99% residual interval was −33.8 to +33.1 µm for photogrammetry and −49.9 to +54.5 µm for handheld scanning; for the unsprayed cylinder, the corresponding intervals were −51.6 to +30.7 µm and −76.3 to +55.3 µm. Sprayed reconstructions in the principal comparison exhibited lower residual dispersion and circularity RMSD. Repeated handheld-scanner acquisitions supported this trend, while supplementary SfM analyses demonstrated the influence of camera-network configuration and calibration treatment on surface-residual dispersion. By linking surface residuals to circularity and centre-offset descriptors, this study provides an empirical basis for interpreting geometric regularity in ancient stone vessels. The results for the tested granite surfaces and workflows highlight the need to distinguish measurement-induced deviations from genuine manufacturing irregularities when analysing polished stone artefacts and ancient vessels.

title: FAME-Net: A Lightweight Feature Alignment and Multi-Scale Enhancement Network for UAV Forest Fire Detection
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing provides a flexible and efficient approach to early forest fire monitoring and warning. However, small fire spots and smoke plumes in UAV imagery vary substantially in texture, morphology, and spatial distribution across scales. Interactions between complex forest backgrounds and target features cause information loss during successive feature compression and misaligned spatial and semantic responses during cross-layer fusion. Limited onboard computing and storage further constrain model complexity. To address these challenges, we propose the lightweight feature alignment and multi-scale enhancement network (FAME-Net), which alleviates feature degradation and response mismatches during encoding and fusion while reducing computational redundancy in multi-scale prediction. At the feature encoding stage, the lightweight multi-scale enhanced backbone (LMEB) combines lightweight downsampling with multi-scale context modeling to reduce computational overhead and preserve fine details of small fire spots and weakly textured smoke. Its hierarchical features are fed into the alignment-aware multi-scale feature fusion neck (AMFF-Neck), which coordinates spatial and semantic responses across scales through cross-layer interactions, reducing fusion bias caused by scale discrepancies and background-induced coupling. The resulting features are processed by the lightweight shared convolution detection head (LSCD), which performs scale alignment, shared convolution, and learnable scale compensation for efficient multi-scale prediction. FAME-Net achieves mAP50 values of 71.5% and 65.3% on the integrated forest fire dataset and the Yuxi Wildfire dataset, respectively, with 1.7 M parameters and 3.9 GFLOPs, indicating a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super (8 GB), it achieves inference speeds of 36.2 and 31.6 FPS on the two datasets, respectively, further supporting its potential for resource-constrained UAV deployment.

title: Whittle–Matérn Roughness Covariance for C-Band SAR Inversion over Bare Agricultural Soil
summary: This study evaluates whether the Whittle–Matérn (WM) covariance representation improves pixel-wise SAR inversion over bare agricultural soil which can exhibit scale-dependent roughness. WM includes a smoothness parameter that controls covariance and roughness spectrum shape and has a Gaussian–Gamma scale-mixture interpretation. It was compared with exponential, Gaussian, and powered exponential (PE) covariance models within the same modified extended advanced integral equation model. Co-registered RADARSAT-2 and Sentinel-1 observations provided five channels for inversion. All experiments used identical observations, ancillary inputs, parameter bounds, objective function, and multi-start optimization settings. The analysis focused on the three co-polarized channels, for which covariance structure enters the scattering model directly. At a co-polarized residual tolerance of 2dB, WM produced model-consistent solutions for 425 of 439 retained pixels, compared with 384, 387, and 423 pixels for the exponential, Gaussian, and PE models, respectively. Its blind point ratio was 3.19%, versus 12.53%, 11.85%, and 3.64%, respectively. On the 342 pixels retrievable by all four models, WM gave the lowest mean absolute error for all channels except Sentinel-1 VH. The largest improvement was obtained for Sentinel-1 VV, where WM reduced RMSE to 0.501dB, compared with 0.820dB, 0.786dB, and 0.606dB for the exponential, Gaussian, and PE models. WM also yielded the most complete retrieval maps and scene mean soil moisture estimates closest to the available SMAP and station reference means. These results show that covariance representation is a material source of structural difference in unregularized multi-sensor SAR inversion.

title: Label Self-Supervised Ship Detection Training Method on One-Bit Non-Reconstructed SAR Images
summary: One-bit quantization technology effectively simplifies the hardware architecture of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and significantly reduces the volume of echo data, making it a pivotal research direction in spaceborne SAR systems. However, the high computational cost and latency associated with one-bit SAR signal reconstruction have limited the efficiency of downstream target detection applications. To address the demand for efficient ship target detection in one-bit SAR imagery, a label self-supervised ship detection training method on one-bit non-reconstructed SAR images is proposed in this paper, which enables generic deep learning models to perform detection directly in one-bit SAR images based on the chirp scaling algorithm (CSA) without signal recovery during inference. First, a training framework based on curriculum learning is designed, aiming to discriminate between real ship targets and false targets. Second, a one-bit reconstruction and training label self-supervised correction branch is incorporated into the training framework to autonomously generate false target labels and progressively guide the model to learn false target features. Third, a one-bit non-reconstructed image dataset is proposed to validate the trained model, which maps only reliable ship target annotations from full-precision echo imaging results. Finally, experiments conducted on real SAR data demonstrate that the detection model derived from the proposed training method can directly detect ship targets in the non-reconstructed images. Compared with the classic “reconstruction-and-detection” workflow, the trained model runs inference, bypassing the reconstruction process, and achieves a 20-fold improvement in efficiency without compromising detection accuracy. This method provides a practical solution for the rapid acquisition of target information in large-scale ship monitoring using one-bit SAR.

title: An Improved Remote-Sensing Mapping Framework for Soil Total Nitrogen in Fog-Prone Regions: Integrating SST Covariates with the XGBoost Model
summary: Monitoring soil total nitrogen (TN) status and spatial variation is essential for preventing land degradation and supporting precision agriculture. Remote sensing (RS) bands and their derived spectral indices are important covariates for soil TN mapping. However, optical RS-based soil mapping may be ineffective in fog-prone regions because water vapor interferes with spectral information. Here, multi-source earth observation data were acquired, including synthetic aperture radar (SAR), multispectral, and topographic data. Spectral indices, SAR-derived indices, and topographic indices related to soil TN were systematically developed. Subsequently, the PCC-VIF method was used to assess the importance of RS-based indices and select the optimal covariates, referred to as SST covariates. Finally, SST covariates and measured soil TN values were used as the independent and dependent variables, respectively, to construct an XGBoost-based soil TN mapping model for regions with persistent foggy cover. The results showed that: (1) SST covariates included Ela, TWI, SOS, VHplusVV, VHdiffVV, B2, and NDGI; (2) the proposed RS-based soil TN mapping model achieved satisfactory accuracy, with an R2 of 0.82 and an RPIQ of 3.03. Compared with models developed using traditional approaches, the R2 increased by approximately 0.16–0.52; and (3) areas with high soil TN content were mainly located in the southern part of the study area, whereas lower TN values occurred in the northern part. Soil TN content and its spatial distribution were mainly influenced by agricultural planting activities and microtopographic conditions. This study provides new insights into RS-based soil TN mapping in fog-prone regions. The robust soil TN mapping framework based on SST covariates and the XGBoost algorithm can support food security and help prevent environmental degradation.

title: Beyond Provincial Averages: A Coupling-Embedded Sustainable Development Index for Multiscale Sustainability Diagnostics in China
summary: Existing environmentally adjusted development indices can assign similar scores to regions with contrasting environmental–social configurations, while provincial averages conceal subprovincial variation. We developed a Coupling-Embedded Sustainable Development Index (CESDI), which retains the Sustainable Development Index (SDI) as baseline performance while incorporating an adjustment for the joint balance and overall development level of the environmental and social subsystems. CESDI was applied to 30 Chinese provincial-level units from 2002 to 2022. Exploratory predictions for 337 Chinese cities were generated using MOSAIKS-inspired Landsat features, nighttime lights, and dual-penalty ridge regression. CESDI preserved the interprovincial SDI gradient (Pearson r = 0.870 to 0.995) while differentiating provinces with similar SDI values but contrasting joint environmental–social conditions. National mean CESDI increased from 0.248 in 2002 to 0.465 in 2017 and declined to 0.371 in 2022. Nested province-grouped cross-validation yielded R2 = 0.4471 and RMSE = 0.1388. Feature-block ablation showed that the dual-penalty model outperformed daytime-only, nighttime-light-only, and equal-penalty specifications. The predicted share of high and very high classes increased from 12.5% to 37.1%, while within-province heterogeneity rose in 21 of 26 multi-unit provinces. The framework integrates baseline sustainability performance with a CCD-defined balance-and-level adjustment and provides an exploratory spatial-screening layer for identifying within-province variation.

title: Multisensor Modeling of Old-Growthness in Mediterranean Pine Forests: New Insights from High-Density Airborne Laser Scanning and Satellite Integration
summary: Old-growth forests (OGFs) are conservation priorities under the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030, but identifying relict stands in Mediterranean Pinus nigra (black pine) forests is challenging due to structural complexity. We evaluated a multisensor remote sensing framework to estimate an Old-Growth Index (OGI) in Cazorla Natural Park (Spain) using high-density Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS) data from the Spanish National Plan for Aerial Orthophotography (PNOA-LiDAR, 2024), RGB–NIR orthophotographs, and multispectral imagery (Sentinel-2 and WorldView-3). Four predictor sets (ALS metrics only; ALS plus canopy cover fraction (CCF); ALS + CCF + Sentinel-2; and ALS + CCF + WorldView-3) were evaluated across Multiple Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Support Vector Regression (SVR) using repeated nested cross-validation. SVR combined with the predictor set ALS + CCF + WorldView-3 achieved the highest nested R2 (0.79), outperforming Random Forest and Multiple Linear Regression. However, models relying solely on ALS (R2 = 0.71) or ALS with CCF (R2 = 0.77) yielded statistically comparable performance. Furthermore, integrating Sentinel-2 (R2 = 0.61–0.68) provided no clear gain over ALS-based models. These findings demonstrate that open-access national LiDAR programs provide sufficient 3D structural information to map stand maturity without requiring commercial satellite imagery. Continuous spatial predictions of OGI offer valuable baseline maps to support conservation planning and OGF monitoring in Mediterranean pine ecosystems.
